title: Neuronal cell-cycle re-entry stratifies clinical trajectories in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis
title_zh: 神经元细胞周期重新进入对肌萎缩侧索硬化症临床进程的分层
abstract: Abstract The clinical heterogeneity of Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS) remains a fundamental barrier to effective therapy. While cell cycle re-entry in post-mitotic neurons is a known precursor to neurodegeneration, its role in defining patient-specific outcomes has never been established. Here, we integrate large-scale transcriptomic profiling from the AnswerALS cohort with mechanistic studies in human iPSC-derived spinal motor neurons to define how cell-cycle re-entry shapes disease heterogeneity in ALS. We identify a transcriptionally distinct patient subgroup with the highest expression of G1 or G2-phase cyclins that exhibit significantly slower functional decline (ALSFRS-R), whereas the engagement of S-phase markers correlates with accelerated disease progression. Nucleocytoplasmic transport dysfunction, a hallmark of ALS and related disorders, disrupts the spatial distribution of key regulatory proteins and may contribute to maladaptive cell-cycle activation. Our recent evidence suggests that impaired nuclear import may initiate, rather than merely accompany, neuronal cell-cycle re-entry. Using iPSC-derived motor neurons, we show that impaired nuclear import initiates TDP-43 pathology and global nuclear/cytoplasmic mis-localization of key ALS-related proteins. This nucleocytoplasmic transport dysfunction triggers a transient wave of cell-cycle activity immediately preceding neuronal cell death. Crucially, we show that DNA-replication initiation is a pathological inflection point of no return, as neurons entering S-phase accumulate replication-associated DNA damage and undergo cell death. Selective inhibition of CDK4/6 prevents S-phase entry and confers potent neuroprotection. Our findings demonstrate that impaired nuclear import drives maladaptive cell-cycle reactivation in ALS and that the depth of cell-cycle engagement stratifies neuronal fate and patient trajectories.
abstract_zh: 摘要 肌萎缩侧索硬化症（ALS）的临床异质性仍然是制约有效治疗的根本障碍。尽管已知后期神经元发生细胞周期重新进入是神经退行性变的前兆，但其在定义患者特异性结局中的作用从未得到证实。在此，我们整合了AnswerALS队列的大规模转录组分析与人源iPSC分化的脊髓运动神经元的机制研究，以阐明细胞周期重新进入如何塑造ALS的疾病异质性。我们鉴定出一个转录特征明确的患者亚组，该亚组G1期或G2期周期素表达最高，且功能衰退（ALSFRS-R）显著较慢；而S期标志物的激活则与疾病进程加快相关。核-胞质转运功能障碍是ALS及相关疾病的标志，它会干扰关键调控蛋白的空间分布，并可能导致细胞周期异常激活。我们近期证据表明，核内转运受损可能启动而非仅伴随神经元细胞周期重新进入。利用iPSC分化的运动神经元，我们表明核内转运受损会启动TDP-43病理及关键ALS相关蛋白的全球性核/胞质错位。这种核-胞质转运功能障碍会引发神经元死亡前立即出现的一过性细胞周期活性波。关键的是，我们证明DNA复制启动是一种不可逆的病理转折点，进入S期的神经元会积累与复制相关的DNA损伤并发生细胞死亡。选择性抑制CDK4/6可阻止S期进入并赋予强大的神经保护作用。我们的研究结果表明，核内转运受损驱动ALS中的适应不良细胞周期重新激活，而细胞周期参与的深度决定了神经元命运和患者进程。
